properties.name: jinja2cpp:used-for
properties.value: nonstd::expected behind jinja2::Result<T> in every Load/Render signature (include/jinja2cpp/template.h, template_env.h); make_unexpected in parsers and bindings

properties.name: jinja2cpp:why
properties.value: C++17 has no std::expected; the 2.0 API returns Result<T> (docs/api-2.0.md decision 4), and Clang 18 + libstdc++ at C++23 ships <expected> without std::expected

properties.name: jinja2cpp:lighten
properties.value: Keep until a C++23 floor. Header-only and small; could be vendored into include/ so consumers need nothing extra, at the cost of an ODR clash with a consumer's own expected-lite of another version

properties.name: jinja2cpp:used-for
properties.value: Python str.format / format filter and %-formatting (src/python_format.cpp, serialize_filters.cpp, value_methods.cpp), number-to-string, wide-string formatting (fmt/xchar.h), error messages (error_info.cpp), the string builder's memory_buffer

properties.name: jinja2cpp:why
properties.value: Python's format-spec mini-language with runtime format strings, precision-as-argument and wchar_t output; std::format is C++20 and the floor is C++17

properties.name: jinja2cpp:lighten
properties.value: Keep. Could be built header-only (FMT_HEADER_ONLY) to remove the link-time dependency of static consumers, at a compile-time cost; replace with std::format only at a C++20 floor (wide output and runtime specs still need checking)
